tasks.task: Plan a community launch or relaunch

items.when: When a community is starting or restarting and needs a purpose, spaces, welcome flow and first weeks
When you want a second plan for starting, growing and turning members into advocates, to compare
When the owner is unsure a community is worth it and wants a small test with costs and measures
When the members are developers and need channels, onboarding and events that suit them
When the launch needs a teaser, a preview for first members and an opening day
When the plan starts with a platform and should start with a few real people who already talk
Before the launch plan is fixed, to compare two plans that place the team's time and budget differently

tasks.task: Set the weekly rhythm and write the posts

items.when: When the community needs repeating weekly formats with the posts written for each
Each week, to run the reply pass, the posts and the monthly read in order
When the owner does not know what to talk about, to find three to five subjects they can keep up
When you want topics drawn from members' own words set out as a calendar, to compare
When each week's posts and questions should feed a plan for the next week
When a prompt got no replies, to see whether it was unseen, skipped or ignored

tasks.task: Reply to a batch of community posts and flag problems

items.when: Daily or a few times a week, to draft replies that get members talking to each other
When the posts worth a reply are picked and each needs an answer that adds something
When a member's situation is delicate and you want a second draft in a different tone
When the same questions come up every week and should become a pinned help page
Before a reply to a complaint is posted, to check every promise, the facts and the tone

tasks.task: Write the welcome message and house rules

items.when: When the community needs rules, each with a reason and an example, that members will read
When new members need a welcome and one small first task
When joining has several steps and members need phased messages and milestones
When the rules are drafted, to put them in plain words without changing what they mean
When rules are written for the loudest members and should ask who does not feel safe to post

tasks.task: Write the moderation playbook: warn, hide, remove, ban

items.when: When moderators need a ladder for each kind of problem and a route for serious harm
When the playbook must match the steps moderators follow in a live incident
When two members are in a running dispute and moderators need a mediation plan
When the worst cases need a first-days plan: who to tell, what to say and what to fix
When moderators step in on everything, to ask who owns the problem before choosing a step

tasks.task: Calm a heated thread without silencing people

items.when: When a thread is turning into an argument or a pile-on and you must decide what to do
When you want short lines for the point people will push back on, to choose from
When one member is furious and needs a reply that names the feeling and promises only what is true
When your own reply sounds sharp, to get a version the member will want to work with
When you are about to correct someone and should first show you heard them accurately

tasks.task: Write removal notices and appeal replies

items.when: After hiding, removing or restricting a post or account, and later when the member appeals
When you need the exact rule and step the notice must quote
Before sending, to make sure the notice is plain and says how to appeal

tasks.task: Handle a moderation incident from report to review

items.when: When a report or flag may be a spam wave, raid, harassment, pile-on or posted personal data
When the incident is public and members need to hear what happened and what changes
After it is over, to turn the timeline into a blameless review and a safer rule or step

tasks.task: Write reply templates for common situations

items.when: When templates for reminders, removals and appeals must match the rules
When recent batches show which situations come up most and need a saved reply
When a situation needs two or three tones to choose from before one is saved
When the set is drafted, to check every template sounds like the community's voice

tasks.task: Set up a moderator rota and induct volunteers

items.when: When volunteer moderators need a fair rota that covers evenings and weekends
When new volunteer moderators need an induction, practice and named supervision
When the induction must teach the ladder and the serious-harm route

tasks.task: Write the monthly community health report

items.when: At the start of each month, to read last month's numbers and choose one or two changes
When the monthly read is one step of the regular cycle
When you have join and activity dates and need to see which groups stay active
When posts and comments must be read for counted themes, with sources
When the report leans on a member survey, to find answers that cannot be trusted

tasks.task: Map outside communities and read their rules

items.when: When a business wants to take part in communities it does not own and needs a map and rules
Before anyone posts in a subreddit, server, group or forum you do not own
When you need a subreddit's real posts and comments in a table to study first
When you need what Reddit, Hacker News and the web are saying about the topic this month

tasks.task: Write a 30-day participation plan and value-first drafts

items.when: When you need a month of honest participation with post and reply drafts
When there are known threads in the category and you must choose which to answer and how
When you want a second Reddit plan with post ideas to compare with yours
Before each draft is posted, to check it against that community's rules on self-promotion
When a draft reads like marketing or a machine and would be called out

tasks.task: Plan an AMA and prepare for hard questions

items.when: When an AMA is in someone else's community and must fit its rules and habits
Before proposing the AMA, to confirm the community allows it and how to ask
When you need the hardest questions people will ask, with honest answers drafted and graded

tasks.task: Design a paid membership offer with levels

items.when: When you need the member promise, one to three levels and the break-even member count
When the levels need prices and a call on flat fee or pay per use
When you want a second three-level ladder with what each includes, to compare
When the promise needs value framing, a guarantee and a name
When there is member data, to check payback and how long members stay against the price

tasks.task: Plan the membership launch and its messages

items.when: When the client wants to start charging, or turn a free group into a paid one
When there is a list and a close date and you need the launch emails planned
When you want three different plans for the email series before writing one
When the membership needs a joining page with promise, proof and price
Before launch, to sort every promise to members into fine, needs proof or cut
Before launch messages are written, to confirm the join link works and the price and levels are live
When the three launch plans are drafted, so a fresh reviewer picks the one to write in full

tasks.task: Map the member journey from joining to renewal

items.when: When you need the path from joining to a first win to renewal
When you know why members cancel and need a plan to get them to a result
When the first two weeks need emails and texts that lead to the first win
When the first visit is confusing and you want a faster path to first value
Each week, to see where new members stall in their first 30 days

tasks.task: Cut cancellations and keep members

items.when: When members leave after month two and you need actions for each stage
When you have cancel data and need the main reasons and where they happen
When you need a cancel flow, save offers and a failed-payment plan
When the cancel page should offer one fitting save per reason
On a schedule, to catch a rise in cancellations early
When the plan chases new joins and the real leak is members who stop coming back

tasks.task: Nudge quiet members back with a personal message

items.when: When members, especially paid ones, have stopped visiting or posting
When you need a weekly list of who is slipping and who is up for renewal
When there are too many quiet members to message and you must rank by risk
Before sending, to cut each nudge to one small thing the member can do

tasks.task: Plan member events and a benefits calendar

items.when: When the 90-day calendar must deliver what each level was promised
When a member event needs a plan to fill seats and follow up
When the benefit is a live session and it needs a teaching outline and slide brief
After an event, to follow up with each member by what they asked

tasks.task: Gather and read member feedback

items.when: When feedback is spread across posts and comments and needs counting by theme
When members' requests for the product must be counted and ruled yes, later or no each week
When you have interviews or survey answers and need patterns in members' own words
Before a member survey goes out, to remove leading questions and plan a pretest

tasks.task: Recognise top contributors and build advocates

items.when: When contributors should earn recognition by reaching a clear level, not by being picked
When paid members could get perks that are not discounts, to compare with status alone
When one member did something worth a short, specific thank-you

always.when: Before rules, notices or launch messages go out, to catch typos and names spelt two ways
When a post or reply states a fact about the product or a member you cannot trace to a source

helpers.when: When threads are really support tickets that need fixing, not conversation
When renewal, win-back and billing emails need building as automated flows
When the launch needs a full email campaign and list work
When a member event is in person or needs suppliers and a run sheet
When membership prices and levels need testing against costs and rivals
When the community's posts must tie into the brand's public social plan

gaps: No library item writes house rules, a moderation ladder, removal notices or appeal replies; only the kit covers moderation
No library item covers a spam wave, raid, harassment or posted personal data, or when to report to the platform or police
No library item sets up Discord, Slack, Facebook group or forum spaces, roles and permissions
No library item writes discussion prompts, polls or a challenge series for a community
No library item writes a set of saved replies for the twenty most common community situations
No library item builds a moderator handover log; the rota item found is for staff shifts
No library item reads community numbers such as active members, first posts and reply times into a health report
No library item reads the rules of a subreddit, server or group and says what is allowed
No library item plans an AMA: timing, host, question collection and follow-up
No library item writes a membership joining page or a 90-day benefits calendar; the page writers found are for products
No library item writes a member newsletter or weekly digest
No library item gives clearly different welcome messages, removal notices or nudges to compare
No library item checks a welcome message, a nudge or house rules before they go out
